reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Mixing Fisher and modified Fisher grades.
name: Fisher Scale

version.label: Original Fisher scale (1980)
version.detail: Grades 1–4. Vasospasm risk peaked at grade 3 and was lower at grade 4. The modified Fisher scale is a different scale and must not be mixed.

purpose: CT classification of subarachnoid blood in relation to vasospasm.
intendedPopulation: Patients with aneurysmal SAH, on the admission CT.

calculatorNotice.title: Non-linear scale
calculatorNotice.message: In the original study, vasospasm was most frequent in grade 3, not grade 4. Many centres now use the modified Fisher scale; state which is used.

options.label: Diffuse or vertical layers under 1 mm
Localised clot and/or vertical layer 1 mm or thicker
Intracerebral or intraventricular clot, with diffuse or no SAH

resultStates.label: Grade 1
resultStates.summary: No subarachnoid blood detected on this CT at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Timing of the CT affects detection.

resultStates.label: Grade 3
resultStates.summary: Localised clot or thick layer: the grade with the highest vasospasm frequency in the original study.
resultStates.detail: Correlate with clinical grade and monitoring according to local protocol.

resultStates.label: Grade 4
resultStates.summary: Intracerebral or intraventricular clot with diffuse or no SAH.

clinicalContext.text: The original CT scale relating subarachnoid blood to vasospasm.

clinicalInsights.text: Report as 'Fisher grade' explicitly to avoid confusion with the modified Fisher scale.

limitations.text: Non-monotonic: risk does not rise steadily with grade.

limitations: Grade 4 treats small and large ventricular clots alike.

confounders.effect: Blood redistributes and clears over time.

guideSections.what: A four-grade CT classification of SAH blood.
guideSections.whenToUse: Admission CT in aneurysmal SAH, where the original scale is used.
guideSections.howToPerform: Choose the grade that best describes the admission CT.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used with clinical grading; specify the scale version.

sources.citation: Fisher CM, Kistler JP, Davis JM. Relation of cerebral vasospasm to subarachnoid hemorrhage visualized by computerized tomographic scanning. Neurosurgery. 1980;6(1):1-9.
